text:
nina: quick proposal to stop postmortem actions from drifting. want a tiny 'due-board' pattern we can reuse.
sam: yes please. the last few PMs had follow-ups that sat for months.
nina: due-board idea (super low ceremony):
```
- Each action gets an ID (A-001) in the postmortem
- Add one-row to the Due Board: id, short title, owner, eta, status, blocker, next_check
- Owners confirm ETA within 48h or it escalates to IC
- Weekly async check-ins until 80% closed (15m max if >5 blocked items)
- After T+30d SRE verifies monitoring, T+60d regression review
```
jess: love the one-row copy/paste. i'll make a tiny sheet and a clipboard-friendly row template.
kai: require single remediation owner. team ownership causes drift. owner transfers must be logged in the row with timestamp.
incident-bot: Reminder set: "dueboard-confirm: db-reconnect-2026" in 48 hours for @nina
sam: propose roles: IC (6-week rotation), Remediation Owner (per action), PM reviewer, SRE verifier. IC has 48h to reassign if owner no-shows.
nina: immediate tasks:
- sheet + row template (jess) 00 due by EOD tomorrow
- add due-board snippet to runbook (sam) 00 due Wed
- start a 6-week IC rotation pilot + sign-up (kai) 00 due next Mon
- tag current open postmortem actions with IDs and add to Due Board (nina) 00 due in 2 days
jess: i'll post sheet link here once ready. small dashboard counts (todo/in-progress/blocked/done) included.
kai: i'll volunteer to run the rotation pilot and take notes for handoff.
sam: how about a simple escalation window: if owner doesn't confirm ETA in 48h -> IC assigns temporary owner and pings team channel. keeps momentum.
nina: agreed. also suggest we automatically set incident-bot reminders for the T+14 and T+30 check-ins.
incident-bot: Reminder set: "dueboard-check: db-reconnect-2026" in 14 days for @nina @kai
jess: sheet will include a tiny 'copy row' button guidance so PMs can paste into postmortems.
sam: let's run this as pilot for the next 2 incidents and iterate. owners, please update your row before weekly checks. low friction = higher compliance.
nina: thanks all. will post plan to #incident-process and file a tiny PR to the runbook after sam's snippet is in.
